title: Cross-repository contract release train and downstream canaries — agent-panel evaluation

panel_protocol.limitation: Source-verified evaluation of release-train manifests, ecosystem lock, consumer-contract suites, schema-surface baselines, and CI workflows; compiler-backed multi-repo builds, live downstream canary runs, and operational release candidate rehearsals remain open gates.

consensus_summary: The multidisciplinary expert evaluation panel reached unanimous consensus approving Track 32 (Cross-repository contract release train and downstream canaries). The core integration and governance assets—including integration/release-train.json, integration/ecosystem-lock.json, release/public-packages.json, contracts/compatibility/schema-surface-0.1.0-alpha.1.json, scripts/check_release_train.py, scripts/sync_ecosystem_lock.py, .github/workflows/integration-release-train.yml, docs/release-train.md, integration/consumer-contract-suite.json, integration/passports/index.json, and tests/test_cross_repository_release_train_governance.py—demonstrate exceptional architectural discipline, fail-closed claim restraint, and robust multi-repository coordination. The release train establishes a strictly contiguous producer-consumer promotion order (1: CiteWeft, 2: Searchright, 3: Sourceright) and enforces default-deny automation across all six lifecycle stages (contract, consumer_fixture, compiler, downstream_canary, release_candidate, promotion). The ecosystem lock fixes observed component identities, cryptographic hashes, and exact commit pins, barring silent background updates. The consumer contract suite coordinates 9 interactions with distinct producer/consumer identities, verified fixture paths, and fail-closed failure semantics that block pin promotion, retain optional adapters, and forbid deleting legacy runtime code in Sourceright. The rollback contract specifies explicit four-step recovery procedures while mandating zero deletion of prior schemas, fixtures, tags, or migration evidence. All public packages remain strictly blocked from publication pending compiler, SemVer, and supply-chain evidence. All 6 governance unit tests and all 6 static checkers pass deterministically network-free. The three higher-evidence operational gates remain preserved as open in the evidence ledger.

assertions_evaluated.notes: Pinned producer-consumer order (CiteWeft -> Searchright -> Sourceright), ecosystem lock, and contiguous stage execution without automatic promotion verified by deterministic checkers and test suites.

Consumer contract suite defines distinct producer/consumer identities, 33 verified fixture paths, and fail-closed failure semantics; CI workflow hardened with read-only permissions and unpersisted credentials.

assertions_evaluated.statement: Explicit promotion, rollback and receipt authority
assertions_evaluated.notes: Explicit four-step rollback procedure, evidence preservation rule, default-deny promotion across all stages, and non-publishable package bounds verified in contracts and test suites.

open_gates.statement: Run compiler-backed consumer contract suites in each producer and consumer repository.
open_gates.evidence: Preserved open until compiler-backed test suites execute across CiteWeft, Searchright, and Sourceright repositories

open_gates.statement: Execute CiteWeft and Sourceright downstream canaries against exact Searchright candidate revisions.
open_gates.evidence: Preserved open until CiteWeft and Sourceright canaries execute against exact candidate pins
